checks.review: Accepted: two curving rivet rows and the buried boat stain clearly connect the iron evidence to the hull outline. Ink, soil, brush, palette and caption clearance match the guide.
Accepted: exactly seven visible flat cartoon men, arranged four plus three; consistent cream faces, closed eyes, capsule clothing and thin limbs. Illustrative layout, not a measured field plan.

Accepted: exactly 34 figures, counted in six bands of 5+6+6+6+6+5. Large burial and small comparison hull read clearly. This organized graphic layout represents the count, not a measured burial arrangement.
Accepted: a simplified upper-arm bone with three visible old impact notches under an amber work lamp; matching ink treatment and cool sample mat, no blood or text.

Accepted after correction: three close burial levels read clearly in a side cutaway. Rejected first draft had mountains; final has a low flat Baltic horizon. Layer count and arrangement are illustrative, not measured reconstruction.
Accepted: overlapping blue/ochre shields physically cover lying men; visible pale heads and thin limbs distinguish covered bodies from stored shields. Contacts and occlusion checked.

Accepted after correction: hands support the folded cloth beside the shield-covered man; a thick exposed arm and smiling expression were replaced by thin graphic limb and neutral mouth. Folded cloth is an illustrative burial-care gesture, not a claimed recovered artifact.

Accepted: burial evidence and plain Lindisfarne church appear in two vignettes on a simple two-point timeline. No date text is burned in; spoken dates belong in captions. Vignettes simplify evidence and architecture.
Accepted: low flat Salme shore, plain clinker boat, two anonymous graphic figures, amber reflection and violet-blue water. No invented fight, perpetrators or certain voyage motive.
